data.narrative:
Humans& is an AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage with five founders including Eric Zelikman and Georges Harik. The valuation landscape for this company spans a heterogeneous universe of 1 public comparable (Palantir Technologies, ticker PLTR) and 8 private peers including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. Given the breadth of business models and development stages across this cohort, traditional peer-median approaches face significant constraints.

Standard peer-median valuation is not applicable to Humans& due to insufficient narrow-stage comparability. Within the 12 same-sector AI & Software peers identified, zero companies share the same development stage, zero occupy adjacent stages, and zero fall within a similar valuation tier. The analytical requirement of at least three datapoints within tightly-filtered categories cannot be satisfied. An all-sector median would introduce substantial measurement error given the wide dispersion in company maturity, revenue generation, and capital efficiency across early-stage AI ventures and mature public software platforms.

The absence of quantitative triangulation methods leaves this valuation fundamentally constrained by data limitations. Forward progress would require either: (1) disclosure of Humans&'s stage and financial metrics to enable stage-filtered peer comparison, or (2) application of alternative methods such as venture cost-of-capital or scenario-based discounted cash flow analysis drawing on disclosed fundraising or operational data. Current public information is insufficient to establish a defensible valuation range.
